findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 1; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶7; figures/FIG-2.md (Side supply passage 30 bullet); figures/FIG-5.md (final relationship bullet)
findings.detail: Claim 1 recites, and the description and two figure briefs repeat, a direct open connection between each side supply passage and the lower return passage. The disclosure never states that these two spaces communicate. It states only that the tray feet leave a return passage under the tray and that the inward spacing of the tray side walls forms the side supply passages, and it routes air from the side supply passages through the tray perforations before the lower return passage. A direct bottom opening between the side passage and the return passage is an undisclosed flow-boundary topology that also creates a bypass around the disclosed perforation route.
findings.evidence: Candidate, claim 1: "each side supply passage extending upward from the lower return passage alongside the removable product tray". Candidate, FIG-2.md: "Side supply passage 30: two blank open upright spaces, each between an upright panel of the tray 20 and the adjacent shell side wall 14, open at the top and, at the bottom, into the lower return passage 28." Candidate, FIG-5.md: "The gap between the tray side wall 24 and the shell side wall 14 is continuous downward with the open space above the shell floor 12 beside the tray foot 22." No affirmative source passage exists. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶5-7: "The product tray is suspended above the shell floor by feet so that a lower return passage remains under the tray. The tray side walls are spaced inward from the shell side walls to form two side supply passages"; "enters the side supply passages, passes through perforations in the product tray, and returns through the lower return passage."
findings.fix: In claim 1, delete "each side supply passage extending upward from the lower return passage alongside the removable product tray," leaving "...to form two side supply passages;". In 08-detailed-description.md ¶7, delete ", each side supply passage 30 extending upward from the lower return passage 28 alongside the removable product tray 20". In FIG-2.md, replace the bullet with "Side supply passage 30: two blank open upright spaces, each between an upright panel of the tray 20 and the adjacent shell side wall 14, open at the top." In FIG-5.md, delete the bullet "The gap between the tray side wall 24 and the shell side wall 14 is continuous downward with the open space above the shell floor 12 beside the tray foot 22."

findings.title: Tray perforations verbalized as located in the upright walls and bottom panel and as opening into both the side supply passage and the lower return passage
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md (Perforation 26 bullet); figures/FIG-2.md (Perforation 26 bullet and flow-arrow bullet)
findings.detail: The disclosure discloses perforations in the product tray but says nothing about which faces of the tray carry them or which passages they open into. The figure briefs verbalize both. Perforations are a functional flow boundary, so under the depiction-convention rule a minimally specific generic opening may be drawn, but the undisclosed relationships must not be verbalized. The description and claims are correctly neutral on this point ("perforations 26 through the removable product tray 20"), so the figure briefs are also inconsistent with the text they illustrate.
findings.evidence: Candidate, FIG-1.md: "Perforation 26: small through holes in the visible upright walls of the tray 20 and in its bottom panel, shown schematically." Candidate, FIG-2.md: "Perforation 26: small gaps through the upright panels and the bottom panel of the tray 20, opening into the adjacent side supply passage 30 and the lower return passage 28." No affirmative source passage exists for either the face assignment or the passage connections. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶7: "passes through perforations in the product tray".
findings.fix: In FIG-1.md, replace the bullet with "Perforation 26: small through holes in the tray 20, shown schematically." In FIG-2.md, replace the bullet with "Perforation 26: small gaps through the tray 20, shown schematically." In FIG-2.md's flow-arrow bullet, replace "down each side supply passage 30, through the perforations 26, and along the lower return passage 28 back into the tray 20" with "down each side supply passage 30, through the perforations 26, and along the lower return passage 28 back into the tray 20" only after the connection language above is removed; that is, leave the arrow sequence but delete the words "opening into the adjacent side supply passage 30 and the lower return passage 28" from the perforation bullet.

findings.title: FIG-3 verbalizes an undisclosed crossover flow path above the upper ends of the cassettes
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md (Phase-change cassette 44 bullet; first relationship bullet)
findings.detail: FIG-3 states that each cassette's upper end is spaced below the frame's upper web and that the space between the cassettes communicates with both guide ducts across the upper parts of the cassettes, so that air turns over the tops of the cassettes into the ducts. The disclosure says only that air "divides along faces of the cassettes" and then "descends through the guide ducts"; it never says where or how the flow crosses from between the cassettes to the ducts beside them. Which end of a cassette the flow passes over, and the existence of a clearance at the upper end, are substantive flow-boundary and end-position statements that the rule requires to be reported even in a schematic view.
findings.evidence: Candidate, FIG-3.md: "each having an outboard surface facing the nearer outboard web and an upper end spaced below the upper web of the frame 42"; "The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 below it and with both ducts 48 across the upper parts of the cassettes 44, so that air entering the opening 46 passes along the opposed faces of the cassettes 44 and turns into the ducts 48." No affirmative source passage exists. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶7: "Warm air rising from the product region enters the central inlet, divides along faces of the cassettes, descends through the guide ducts".
findings.fix: In FIG-3.md, delete " and an upper end spaced below the upper web of the frame 42" from the cassette bullet, and replace the first relationship bullet with "The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 below it and communicates with both ducts 48, so that air entering the opening 46 passes along the opposed faces of the cassettes 44 and into the ducts 48."

findings.title: Shallow condensate channel 70 verbalized as a trough formed in the upper surface of the shell floor at the lower end of the side supply passage
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (Shell floor 12 bullet); figures/FIG-5.md (Shallow condensate channel 70 bullet)
findings.detail: The disclosure locates the condensate channel only as being "around the product tray". The figure briefs verbalize it as a trough formed in the upper surface of the shell floor, positioned between the foot of the shell side wall and the lower end of the tray side wall, i.e. inside the lower end of the side supply passage. That is an undisclosed relative location for a functional flow feature and it places the channel in the air circulation path. Drawing the channel as a generic shallow upwardly open trough is a permissible depiction convention; verbalizing where it is formed and what it lies between is not.
findings.evidence: Candidate, FIG-5.md: "Shallow condensate channel 70: an upwardly open trough in the upper surface of the shell floor 12, between the foot of the shell side wall 14 and the lower end of the tray side wall 24, its depth small compared with its width." Candidate, FIG-2.md: "Shell floor 12: a horizontal hatched slab spanning the bottom of the view, its upper surface carrying a shallow upwardly open trough at each side beside the adjacent shell side wall 14." No affirmative source passage exists. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶11: "A removable absorbent wick lies in a shallow condensate channel around the product tray."
findings.fix: In FIG-5.md, replace the bullet with "Shallow condensate channel 70: a shallow upwardly open trough alongside the removable product tray, shown schematically, its depth small compared with its width." In FIG-2.md, replace the Shell floor 12 bullet with "Shell floor 12: a horizontal hatched slab spanning the bottom of the view." and, if the channel must be indicated in FIG-2, add "A shallow upwardly open trough is shown schematically alongside the tray 20 at each side."

findings.title: Condensate discharge opening 56 verbalized as discharging into the side supply passage rather than into the condensate channel
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md (Condensate discharge opening 56 bullet)
findings.detail: FIG-4 states that opening 56 opens downward above the upper end of side supply passage 30. The disclosure states that the openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate into the channel. FIG-4's wording is both untraced and inconsistent with 08-detailed-description.md ¶39 and claim 6, which recite discharge into the shallow condensate channel. It also creates a flow path in which condensate falls the full height of the side supply passage, a relationship the inventor never described.
findings.evidence: Candidate, FIG-4.md: "Condensate discharge opening 56: a downwardly opening gap at the lower end of the duct 48 in the underside of the frame 42, opening downward above the upper end of the side supply passage 30." Contradicted text, 08-detailed-description.md ¶39: "Condensate discharge openings 56 at lower ends of the downward guide ducts 48 discharge condensate into the shallow condensate channel 70." No affirmative source passage supports the FIG-4 wording. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶11: "Openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate into the channel."
findings.fix: In FIG-4.md, replace the bullet with "Condensate discharge opening 56: a downwardly opening gap at the lower end of the duct 48 in the underside of the frame 42, shown schematically."

findings.title: FIG-6 verbalizes an undisclosed gap between the indicator stem and the phase-change cassette while asserting thermal coupling
findings.where: figures/FIG-6.md (Indicator stem 82 bullet; Phase-change cassette 44 bullet; first relationship bullet)
findings.detail: FIG-6 fixes the inner end of stem 82 at the inner surface of the shell side wall and places cassette 44 spaced inboard of that surface, while simultaneously stating that the stem is thermally coupled to the facing surface of the cassette. The disclosure says only that the stem is "thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette". Whether the coupling is by contact or across a gap, where the stem terminates, and how far the cassette stands off the wall are contact-topology and relative-location statements that convey technical substance and are untraced. The wording is also internally strained, asserting coupling to a facing surface that it has just placed at a distance.
findings.evidence: Candidate, FIG-6.md: "Its inner end lies at the inner surface of the shell side wall 14 and its outer end lies inside the housing, short of the closed outer end"; "Phase-change cassette 44: a slab-like body inside the carrier at the right of the view ... spaced inboard of the inner surface of the shell side wall 14, the inner end of the stem 82 lying at that inner surface and thermally coupled to the facing surface of the cassette 44." No affirmative source passage exists. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶13: "An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch."
findings.fix: In FIG-6.md, replace the stem bullet's terminal clause with "Its inner end lies at the inner side of the shell side wall 14 and its outer end lies inside the housing." Replace the cassette bullet with "Phase-change cassette 44: a slab-like body inside the carrier at the right of the view, drawn with its own outline and its own hatching pattern, the inner end of the stem 82 being thermally coupled to it." Replace the first relationship bullet with "The stem 82 extends from the interior of the indicator 80 through the thickness of the shell side wall 14, where it is thermally coupled to the cassette 44."

findings.title: FIG-6 places a phase-change cassette directly against the shell side wall, contradicting FIG-2, FIG-3 and FIG-4
findings.where: figures/FIG-6.md (Phase-change cassette 44 bullet); figures/FIG-2.md (left-hand detail circle); figures/FIG-3.md; figures/FIG-4.md
findings.detail: FIG-6 shows cassette 44 immediately inboard of the inner surface of the shell side wall with nothing between them. FIG-3 places each cassette inboard of guide duct 48, which is in turn inboard of the frame's outboard web; FIG-4 places the frame's outboard web inboard of the shell side wall with side supply passage 30 below. FIG-2 identifies the left-hand detail circle as the shell side wall with its housing and bore, at a location where the adjacent inboard space is the side supply passage and the tray, not a cassette. The same numeral 44 therefore appears in two mutually inconsistent positions relative to the shell wall.
findings.evidence: FIG-6.md: cassette 44 "spaced inboard of the inner surface of the shell side wall 14". FIG-3.md: "Downward guide duct 48: two blank open upright passages, one on each side, each between the outboard surface of one cassette 44 and the nearer outboard web of the frame 42". FIG-4.md: "Rigid spacer frame 42: ... the outboard web lying inboard of the shell side wall 14" and "Downward guide duct 48: a blank open upright passage inboard of the outboard web of the frame 42". FIG-2.md: the fourth circle is "the left shell side wall 14 with its housing and bore."
findings.fix: In FIG-6.md, show the cassette 44 without asserting adjacency to the wall: replace "a slab-like body inside the carrier at the right of the view ... spaced inboard of the inner surface of the shell side wall 14" with "a slab-like body of the removable thermal module shown at the right of the view, drawn with its own outline and its own hatching pattern, the inner end of the stem 82 being thermally coupled to it, intervening structure between the shell side wall 14 and the cassette 44 being omitted for clarity." Add to FIG-6.md's opening paragraph: "Structure between the shell side wall 14 and the cassette 44 is omitted for clarity."

findings.title: Sectional figures show the closed lid resting directly on the shell side walls, omitting and contradicting compressible lid gasket 64
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (Insulated lid 60 bullet); figures/FIG-3.md (Insulated lid 60 bullet); figures/FIG-4.md (unnumbered slab bullets)
findings.detail: All three sectional views depict the carrier in the closed condition, and FIG-2 and FIG-4 affirmatively state that the lid rests across or on the shell side walls. The description and claim 2 require that in the closed condition the compressible lid gasket 64 is compressed between the lid and upper edge 16. No sectional brief shows or accounts for the gasket, and the "resting on" wording asserts direct lid-to-wall contact that the text excludes.
findings.evidence: Candidate, FIG-2.md: "Insulated lid 60: a horizontal hatched slab closing the top of the view, resting across both shell side walls 14 above the module 40." Candidate, FIG-4.md: "An unnumbered horizontal hatched slab of substantial thickness spans the top of the view and rests on the upper end of the shell side wall 14." Contradicted text, 08-detailed-description.md ¶31: "Only then does continued closing compress the compressible lid gasket 64 against the upper edge 16 and seal the interior."
findings.fix: In FIG-2.md, replace with "Insulated lid 60: a horizontal hatched slab closing the top of the view above the module 40, a compressible lid gasket 64 being compressed between its underside and the upper edge of each shell side wall 14," and add 64 to that brief's numeral list. In FIG-4.md, replace the two unnumbered-slab statements with "Insulated lid 60: a horizontal hatched slab of substantial thickness spanning the top of the view, a compressible lid gasket 64 being compressed between its underside and the upper end of the shell side wall 14" and "The lid 60 lies above the frame 42 while the foot 54 sits on the ledge 18," and add 60 and 64 to that brief's numeral list.

findings.title: FIG-2 routes air downward out of the module's descending passages into the side supply passages, bypassing peripheral outlet openings 50
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (Removable thermal module 40 bullet; flow-arrow bullet)
findings.detail: FIG-2 states that each descending passage of the module opens downward above one side supply passage and that the flow arrows run straight down from those passages into the side supply passages. The claims and description require the air to leave the guide ducts sideways through peripheral outlet openings 50, whose overlap with the side supply passages is the whole point of registration, and FIG-4 depicts exactly that. FIG-2 therefore shows a flow route in which the registered overlap plays no part.
findings.evidence: Candidate, FIG-2.md: "two unnumbered descending passages either side of that opening, each opening downward above one side supply passage 30"; flow arrows "down its two descending passages, down each side supply passage 30". Contradicted text, claim 12: "downward through the downward guide ducts, through the peripheral outlet openings into the side supply passages"; FIG-4.md: "The duct 48 opens sideways through the peripheral outlet opening 50, and the opening 50 overlaps the upper end of the side supply passage 30 so that the two are in open communication."
findings.fix: In FIG-2.md, replace "each opening downward above one side supply passage 30" with "each communicating at its lower end with one side supply passage 30 through a peripheral outlet opening 50 of the module 40", and replace the corresponding arrow wording with "down its two descending passages, through the peripheral outlet openings 50 into the side supply passages 30, down each side supply passage 30". Add 50 to that brief's numeral list.

findings.title: Description extends insulating construction to "the walls that bound the interior"
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶5
findings.detail: The disclosure identifies an insulated outer shell and an insulated lid. It says nothing about the construction of any other wall bounding the interior, such as the tray side walls or the spacer frame webs. The added clause asserts a material property for parts the inventor never characterized.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The insulated outer shell 10, the insulated lid 60, and the walls that bound the interior are of insulating construction, so that the carrier can be returned for reuse." No affirmative source passage exists. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶5: "A reusable passive cold-chain carrier has an insulated outer shell, a removable product tray, a removable thermal module, and an insulated lid."
findings.fix: Replace with "The insulated outer shell 10 and the insulated lid 60 are of insulating construction, and the carrier can be returned for reuse."

findings.title: Description adds "without dismantling the removable thermal module 40" to the wick-replacement result
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶41
findings.detail: The disclosure states only that the wick can be replaced without opening a phase-change cassette. The added phrase asserts a second, broader servicing result the inventor did not state.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "so that the removable absorbent wick 72 is drawn out of the shallow condensate channel 70 and replaced without opening a phase-change cassette 44 and without dismantling the removable thermal module 40." No affirmative source passage exists. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶11: "allowing the wick to be replaced without opening a phase-change cassette."
findings.fix: Delete " and without dismantling the removable thermal module 40".

findings.title: Cassettes characterized as "sealed" and as being "returned for conditioning"
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶15, ¶41, ¶55
findings.detail: The disclosure calls the cassettes phase-change cassettes that are conditioned before use and that should not be opened when the wick is replaced. It does not characterize them as sealed, nor does it describe returning them for conditioning as a servicing step. These are draft-supplied characterizations. The word "sealed" also appears in the Background as the draft's own prose, which is not inventor support.
findings.evidence: Candidate ¶15: "Each phase-change cassette 44 is a sealed cassette of phase-change material that is conditioned before use". Candidate ¶41: "the sealed phase-change cassettes 44, which are conditioned items that should be returned to conditioning intact." Candidate ¶55: "the phase-change cassettes 44 are returned for conditioning". Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶11 and ¶15: "without opening a phase-change cassette"; "conditioned cassettes are fitted to the spacer frame".
findings.fix: In ¶15, replace with "Each phase-change cassette 44 is a cassette of phase-change material that is conditioned before use." In ¶41, replace "the sealed phase-change cassettes 44, which are conditioned items that should be returned to conditioning intact" with "the phase-change cassettes 44, which are conditioned items and are not to be opened." In ¶55, replace "the phase-change cassettes 44 are returned for conditioning" with "the phase-change cassettes 44 are reconditioned".

findings.title: FIG-3 verbalizes cassettes "of equal size" and locates mating channel 52 "to one side of the opening 46"
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md (Phase-change cassette 44 bullet; Mating channel 52 bullet)
findings.detail: The disclosure states that the frame holds two opposed cassettes and that the frame has a mating channel, without specifying relative cassette size or where on the frame the channel lies. Equal size is a verbalized proportion, and "to one side of the opening 46" is a verbalized circumferential position for a functional joint. Drawing two similar slabs and a recess somewhere on the upper web is a permissible convention; stating the proportion and the end position is not.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Phase-change cassette 44: two upright slab-like bodies of equal size held within the frame 42"; "Mating channel 52: an upwardly open recess in the upper web of the frame 42, to one side of the opening 46 and bounded on both sides by hatched frame material." No affirmative source passage exists. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶7 and ¶9: "a rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes"; "the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame".
findings.fix: In FIG-3.md, delete " of equal size" from the cassette bullet, and replace the mating channel bullet with "Mating channel 52: an upwardly open recess in the upper web of the frame 42, shown schematically and bounded on both sides by hatched frame material."

structured_output.summary:
Preflight source-fidelity review of the p14 passive cold-chain carrier draft against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (the two are textually identical; there is no second USER message, so the ledger authority is one paragraph block).

Filing formalities check out. The title, "Not applicable" cross-reference and "Not applicable" government-support statement match input/brief.md ("No priority claim. No federally sponsored research or development."). No means-plus-function language appears. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain in any draft file. The abstract is 140 words, within the 150-word limit. The reference-numeral table is internally consistent: every numeral in numerals.md is used in the description, each numeral denotes exactly one part, and each figure brief's "Numerals shown on this figure" list matches the items actually verbalized in that brief. The section-line designation is consistent across all three places it must appear: FIG-1.md defines "line 2-2 ... the same section designation being repeated at each end of the line", FIG-2.md is "taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 1", and draft/07-drawings.md recites "taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 1". The four detail circles in FIG-2.md are unnumbered and are referred to by consistent positional wording in 07-drawings.md.

The independent-claim backbone traces cleanly. Every element of claim 1 and claim 12 other than the item in Finding 1 is affirmatively disclosed, including the shell/tray/module/lid architecture, tray feet and lower return passage, tray side walls spaced inward to form two side supply passages, the rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes, the central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes, peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages, the full circulation sequence, the "no fan, pump, or powered air mover" negative limitation, and lid-driven registration by the depending indexing rib entering the mating channel. Dependent claims 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 17 each trace to an exact sentence in the disclosure. Claims 5 and 15 (module lifts out as one piece with both cassettes; tray thereafter lifts out with the payload) follow directly from the disclosed removability and stacking order and are treated as supported. The optional-feature framing in the Summary and the Variations paragraph matches the disclosure's own statement that "The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features."

Thirteen findings follow. Six are critical disclosure_fidelity items, all of them verbalized geometric or flow relationships that the inventor never stated. Every one is in a functional flow boundary or contact interface, so the schematic-depiction allowance does not cover them: which passages the tray perforations open into; the side supply passages opening at their lower ends directly into the lower return passage (this one is also a claim 1 limitation, and it creates an undisclosed bypass around the disclosed perforation route); the crossover above the upper ends of the cassettes by which FIG-3 routes air from between the cassettes into the outboard ducts; the condensate channel verbalized as a trough formed in the upper surface of the shell floor between the shell wall foot and the tray wall; condensate discharge opening 56 verbalized as discharging into the side supply passage rather than into the channel, which also contradicts the disclosure's own "discharge condensate into the channel"; and the FIG-6 statement that the indicator stem ends at the wall's inner surface with the cassette spaced inboard of it, which asserts a specific non-contact coupling gap. In each case the underlying part is disclosed, so the fix strips the verbalized relationship and keeps a minimally specific generic depiction; no fix adds a speculative shape or a new optional embodiment to the application text.

Three findings are major internal_logic inconsistencies among the figure briefs. FIG-6 places a phase-change cassette directly facing the inner surface of the shell side wall, which cannot be reconciled with FIG-3 and FIG-4, where each cassette is separated from the shell wall by guide duct 48 and the frame's outboard web, or with FIG-2, where the module sits above the tray and the space beside the shell wall is the side supply passage. FIG-2, FIG-3 and FIG-4 all show the closed carrier with the lid resting directly on the shell side walls and omit compressible lid gasket 64, contradicting the description's statement that closing compresses the gasket against upper edge 16. FIG-2 routes the descending module passages downward directly into the side supply passages, bypassing the peripheral outlet openings 50 through which claim 12 and the description require the air to pass.

Four minor findings cover small unsupported characterizations in the description ("the walls that bound the interior are of insulating construction"; "without dismantling the removable thermal module 40"; the "sealed" and "returned for conditioning" cassette characterizations) and two verbalized geometric choices in FIG-3 (cassettes "of equal size"; mating channel "to one side of the opening 46").

Background prior-art characterizations were not assessed for inventor support, per the standing instruction; they contain no citations for a later reviewer to trace. Per input/brief.md, no prior-art search was run and the art in prior_art/ may be incomplete.

findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (Insulated lid 60 bullet); figures/FIG-3.md (Insulated lid 60 bullet); figures/FIG-4.md (unnumbered slab bullets)
findings.detail: All three sectional views depict the carrier in the closed condition, and FIG-2 and FIG-4 affirmatively state that the lid rests across or on the shell side walls. The description and claim 2 require that in the closed condition the compressible lid gasket 64 is compressed between the lid and upper edge 16. No sectional brief shows or accounts for the gasket, and the "resting on" wording asserts direct lid-to-wall contact that the text excludes.
findings.evidence: Candidate, FIG-2.md: "Insulated lid 60: a horizontal hatched slab closing the top of the view, resting across both shell side walls 14 above the module 40." Candidate, FIG-4.md: "An unnumbered horizontal hatched slab of substantial thickness spans the top of the view and rests on the upper end of the shell side wall 14." Contradicted text, 08-detailed-description.md ¶31: "Only then does continued closing compress the compressible lid gasket 64 against the upper edge 16 and seal the interior."
findings.fix: In FIG-2.md, replace with "Insulated lid 60: a horizontal hatched slab closing the top of the view above the module 40, a compressible lid gasket 64 being compressed between its underside and the upper edge of each shell side wall 14," and add 64 to that brief's numeral list. In FIG-4.md, replace the two unnumbered-slab statements with "Insulated lid 60: a horizontal hatched slab of substantial thickness spanning the top of the view, a compressible lid gasket 64 being compressed between its underside and the upper end of the shell side wall 14" and "The lid 60 lies above the frame 42 while the foot 54 sits on the ledge 18," and add 60 and 64 to that brief's numeral list.

findings.title: FIG-2 routes air downward out of the module's descending passages into the side supply passages, bypassing peripheral outlet openings 50
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (Removable thermal module 40 bullet; flow-arrow bullet)
findings.detail: FIG-2 states that each descending passage of the module opens downward above one side supply passage and that the flow arrows run straight down from those passages into the side supply passages. The claims and description require the air to leave the guide ducts sideways through peripheral outlet openings 50, whose overlap with the side supply passages is the whole point of registration, and FIG-4 depicts exactly that. FIG-2 therefore shows a flow route in which the registered overlap plays no part.
findings.evidence: Candidate, FIG-2.md: "two unnumbered descending passages either side of that opening, each opening downward above one side supply passage 30"; flow arrows "down its two descending passages, down each side supply passage 30". Contradicted text, claim 12: "downward through the downward guide ducts, through the peripheral outlet openings into the side supply passages"; FIG-4.md: "The duct 48 opens sideways through the peripheral outlet opening 50, and the opening 50 overlaps the upper end of the side supply passage 30 so that the two are in open communication."
findings.fix: In FIG-2.md, replace "each opening downward above one side supply passage 30" with "each communicating at its lower end with one side supply passage 30 through a peripheral outlet opening 50 of the module 40", and replace the corresponding arrow wording with "down its two descending passages, through the peripheral outlet openings 50 into the side supply passages 30, down each side supply passage 30". Add 50 to that brief's numeral list.

findings.title: Description extends insulating construction to "the walls that bound the interior"
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶5
findings.detail: The disclosure identifies an insulated outer shell and an insulated lid. It says nothing about the construction of any other wall bounding the interior, such as the tray side walls or the spacer frame webs. The added clause asserts a material property for parts the inventor never characterized.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The insulated outer shell 10, the insulated lid 60, and the walls that bound the interior are of insulating construction, so that the carrier can be returned for reuse." No affirmative source passage exists. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶5: "A reusable passive cold-chain carrier has an insulated outer shell, a removable product tray, a removable thermal module, and an insulated lid."
findings.fix: Replace with "The insulated outer shell 10 and the insulated lid 60 are of insulating construction, and the carrier can be returned for reuse."

findings.title: Description adds "without dismantling the removable thermal module 40" to the wick-replacement result
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶41
findings.detail: The disclosure states only that the wick can be replaced without opening a phase-change cassette. The added phrase asserts a second, broader servicing result the inventor did not state.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "so that the removable absorbent wick 72 is drawn out of the shallow condensate channel 70 and replaced without opening a phase-change cassette 44 and without dismantling the removable thermal module 40." No affirmative source passage exists. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶11: "allowing the wick to be replaced without opening a phase-change cassette."
findings.fix: Delete " and without dismantling the removable thermal module 40".

findings.title: Cassettes characterized as "sealed" and as being "returned for conditioning"
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶15, ¶41, ¶55
findings.detail: The disclosure calls the cassettes phase-change cassettes that are conditioned before use and that should not be opened when the wick is replaced. It does not characterize them as sealed, nor does it describe returning them for conditioning as a servicing step. These are draft-supplied characterizations. The word "sealed" also appears in the Background as the draft's own prose, which is not inventor support.
findings.evidence: Candidate ¶15: "Each phase-change cassette 44 is a sealed cassette of phase-change material that is conditioned before use". Candidate ¶41: "the sealed phase-change cassettes 44, which are conditioned items that should be returned to conditioning intact." Candidate ¶55: "the phase-change cassettes 44 are returned for conditioning". Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶11 and ¶15: "without opening a phase-change cassette"; "conditioned cassettes are fitted to the spacer frame".
findings.fix: In ¶15, replace with "Each phase-change cassette 44 is a cassette of phase-change material that is conditioned before use." In ¶41, replace "the sealed phase-change cassettes 44, which are conditioned items that should be returned to conditioning intact" with "the phase-change cassettes 44, which are conditioned items and are not to be opened." In ¶55, replace "the phase-change cassettes 44 are returned for conditioning" with "the phase-change cassettes 44 are reconditioned".

findings.title: FIG-3 verbalizes cassettes "of equal size" and locates mating channel 52 "to one side of the opening 46"
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md (Phase-change cassette 44 bullet; Mating channel 52 bullet)
findings.detail: The disclosure states that the frame holds two opposed cassettes and that the frame has a mating channel, without specifying relative cassette size or where on the frame the channel lies. Equal size is a verbalized proportion, and "to one side of the opening 46" is a verbalized circumferential position for a functional joint. Drawing two similar slabs and a recess somewhere on the upper web is a permissible convention; stating the proportion and the end position is not.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Phase-change cassette 44: two upright slab-like bodies of equal size held within the frame 42"; "Mating channel 52: an upwardly open recess in the upper web of the frame 42, to one side of the opening 46 and bounded on both sides by hatched frame material." No affirmative source passage exists. Nearest source, disclosure.md ¶7 and ¶9: "a rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes"; "the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame".
findings.fix: In FIG-3.md, delete " of equal size" from the cassette bullet, and replace the mating channel bullet with "Mating channel 52: an upwardly open recess in the upper web of the frame 42, shown schematically and bounded on both sides by hatched frame material."
